question: Which Sultan established a separate department (Diwan-i-Amir Kohi) to take care of agriculture?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Bin Tughlaq.**__

__
 
• **Muhammad Bin Tughlaq** established a separate department (Diwan-i-Amir Kohi) to take care of **agriculture.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Bin Tughlaq** created a department of agriculture known as **Diwan-i-Kohi.**

 
 
• The main object of the department was to **increase** the** land under cultivation. **
 
 
 
• Under the **Diwan-i-Kohi** loans were advanced to farmers for the **purchase of cattle, seeds**, and** digging of wells **but to no avail.
 
• **Mohammad Bin Tuglaq:**__
 __
 
• **Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq** pushed for** India's administrative** and **political union**.
 
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** ascended the **throne** of the **Tughlaq dynasty** of **Delhi** in **February 1325 CE**.
 
• In** 1327**, Tughluq ordered to move his **capital **from **Delhi** to **Daulatabad **in the **Deccan region **of** India.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Person Name**
 **Details**
 
 

 **Khizr Khan**
 
 
 
• Khizr Khan was the founder of the Sayyid dynasty, the ruling dynasty of the Delhi sultanate, in northern India soon after the invasion of Timur and the fall of the Tughlaq dynasty.
 
• Khan was Governor of Multan under the Tughlaq ruler, Firuz Shah Tughlaq, and was known to be an able administrator.
 
 
 
 

 **Jalal-ud-din-Khalji**
 
 
 
• Jalal-ud-din Khalji was the founder and first Sultan of the Khalji dynasty that ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1290 to 1320.
 
• Jalal-ud-din, ascended the throne of Delhi in June 1290, at the unfinished Kilokhri Palace near Delhi.
 
 
 
 

 **Tughril Beg**
 
 
 
• Tughril Beg was the founder Seljuk Empire.
 
• Tughril Beg was the Sultan of the Great Seljuk Empire until his death in 1063.
